verdict.rationale: Honeybadger documents official client libraries that automatically report errors once installed. The evidence explicitly covers a Python backend SDK and a Cocoa mobile SDK. Web frontend coverage rests only on JS package changelogs (automatic HTTP instrumentation) and source-map un-minification, with no explicit statement that the JS SDK auto-captures uncaught browser errors. Missing for 10: explicit documentation of automatic uncaught-error capture in the browser/JS SDK, evidence of Android or other mobile SDKs beyond Cocoa, and independent or hands-on corroboration of automatic capture across platforms.

support.subject: As a developer, I can instrument my web frontend, backend services, and mobile apps with official SDKs that capture uncaught errors automatically

citations.quote: Once our client library is installed and configured, errors thrown by your application are automatically sent to our API.
Once installed, Honeybadger will automatically report crashes and errors in your app.
Once installed, Honeybadger will automatically report errors and telemetry in your Python application.
Capture HTTP requests with automatic instrumentation and take advantage of new configuration options for event correlation, event context, handlers, and more with the updates for our JS packages.
